title: Detecting Collisions
summary: The collision tests 2D games are built on - point in rectangle, rectangle against rectangle, circle against circle and circle against rectangle - how each one works, raylib's functions for them, and choosing the right shape for each object.

cards.a: An axis-aligned bounding box: a rectangle whose sides are parallel to the x and y axes.

cards.q: Why compare squared distances for circles?
cards.a: It gives the same answer as comparing distances, without the cost of a square root.

cards.q: How do you test a circle against a rectangle?
cards.a: Clamp the circle's centre to the rectangle to find the closest point, and check whether that point is within the radius.
